commits.subject: Route local MCP board notifications through response item injection (#62302)
commits.reason: Carry the local MCP board’s opted-in delivery through the same native receiver queue used for ordinary plaintext agent mail. Keep board membership, backend ownership and the fork’s manager-wide admission in their existing owners.
evidence: LocalBoardHost chooses injection only when the MCP feature provisions the board and there is no explicit LocalBoardConnection. It requires an already loaded receiver reporting Multi-Agent v2 and enabled native tools. Other modes keep direct InterAgentCommunication submission. The local_board_host constructor remains native.

The host resolves the recipient through its exact board connection or tree, then resolves its registered agent path. It builds one queue-only notice from the original post author, that path and the post preview text. The remote-notification wrapper retains the existing size bound. A missing receiver is skipped without starting or reloading a thread.

The feature HTTP scenario now compares the entire list of matching notices with one item from /root/worker to /root carrying the canonical channel-post text. The same run checks the stored board read and author. An accepted notification reports Core submission, independently of durable post storage.

Core’s preceding plaintext-injection change owns conversion, delivery-phase handling and the interaction with manager handoff. The board sends exactly one item and does not create a sender publication or terminal-result writer. Explicit-retention RPC and retained Side remain on their separate typed entry point.

Four native Core HTTP scenarios passed on f1d3274f0c02313a9b769927193d25af3eaafc05 using Trust 15698 and the source-built message-board executable. The feature route delivered exactly one canonical /root/worker to /root post notification and the durable read retained its author. Configured, plugin and in-memory boards also passed. The test image SHA-256 was 3175686c47e87addb5450cd9caae3883a84a4a0832284aa004d91512f460fb6f.
commits.revisit: Repeat the actual child-post and root-read HTTP scenarios across feature-provisioned and explicitly configured backends when board routing or receiver identity changes. Recheck inactive receivers and the remote notification budget if delivery policy changes.
